hook: Extreme macro close-up of dull/tan skin being wiped, with a bold 'Before / After' label printed directly over the skin split — instantly promises a visible transformation in the first 1s.

copy.headline: Get visibly lighter skin INSTANTLY!
copy.primary_text_summary: Instant Spotlite Mask fades dark spots in 10 mins; for underarms, neck & body. Tap to get yours.

visual.composition: Vertical full-bleed macro of skin/limb; label text overlaid on the body; satisfying hands-applying-cream ASMR mid-section
visual.typography_feel: bold condensed sans, sticker/handwritten arrow accents

video_structure.shot: hands massaging white cream, product reveal

why_it_likely_works: Leads with a visceral before/after on the exact body area, promising a fast, measurable result — the macro ASMR demo keeps watch-time high. Live 145 days = strong signal.
weaknesses: Skin-lightening framing is category-crowded and can read as a borderline claim; no strong brand world beyond the demo.

hook: A relatable young woman films herself at home holding the tube to camera with sticker text 'Testing the viral Sanfe…' — pure native creator reel energy; an AC unit visible behind her signals the Indian-heat context.

copy.headline: creator reel (khushiyaannn)
copy.primary_text_summary: 'I love quick results' — 2-minute tan remover got rid of dead skin and darkness; self-care/growth-era framing; heavy hashtags.

visual.composition: Handheld selfie-distance portrait, product held beside face, lo-fi bedroom
visual.setting: home bedroom, AC + flowers in frame

why_it_likely_works: Feels like organic content, not an ad; creator trust + 'in 2 minutes' speed + a self-care narrative that fits Gen-Z. Partnership/creator format is Sanfe's dominant, repeated play.
weaknesses: Depends on creator credibility; product barely shown in detail; claim-heavy.

hook: Opens on a direct question 'Still struggling with facial hair?' with embarrassed emojis — names the insecurity in the first line.

hook: A stylish young man in a sporty jersey in a design-forward room picks up the trimmer box — aspirational-but-relatable male grooming world in the first 2s.

visual.composition: Hero prop styling, product nested in themed food prop, outdoor picnic

why_it_likely_works: Playful food-mood styling makes a tiny product scroll-stopping and shareable; flavour-as-mood naming is distinctive.
weaknesses: Adjacent category (lip, not body); pure vibe, no claim/benefit.

hook: 'INDIA'S MOST WANTED LOTION IS BACK!' over old-vs-new bottles, plus a mock 'WARNING: Criminally smooth glow-up noticed' — hype + playful cop/warning meme.

copy.headline: India's Most Wanted Lotion Is Back!
copy.primary_text_summary: Returning hero lotion (Vanilla Caramello), reformulated with cocoa butter / hyaluronic; 'dessert o'clock round the clock' lifestyle slide.

visual.composition: Slide1 old→new bottle with arrow + warning bar; slide2 model holding bottle, lotion heart on skin, cutout on purple + bakery backdrop

why_it_likely_works: 'Most wanted / back in stock' manufactures demand and FOMO; meme-y warning bar adds Gen-Z humour; carousel lets old→new→lifestyle tell a mini story. Duplicate creative = scaling.
weaknesses: Relies on prior brand fame ('is back'), harder for a newer brand to borrow literally.

hook: 'build your skincare routine at flat ₹599' with a clean clinical product trio on water/stone and a FREE GIFT flag.
